title: Working at Redwood — Roles, Career Ladders, Benefits, Hiring & Onboarding Guide
author: Ava Martinez
body:
Overview

Welcome to Redwood Inference. This document is the canonical company handbook reference covering what it's like to work at Redwood, our role and career ladder structure, benefits and perks, a high-level hiring and onboarding overview, and the core internal tools new hires will use. It is maintained by People Ops and updated periodically; see the 'Related pages' links for deeper policy pages.

1) Working at Redwood — principles and culture

- Our mission: Make high-performance, reliable LLM inference accessible to every engineering team. We hire and work toward that mission with a product- and engineering-first mindset.
- Core values: Engineering excellence, customer empathy, ownership, inclusive collaboration, and operational rigor.
- Expectations: Ship iteratively, practice blameless postmortems, document decisions (ADRs), and prioritize reliability and cost-efficiency for production systems.
- Working model: Hybrid-first. Teams define weekly sync expectations; core hours are 11:00–16:00 PT for cross-team collaboration. People managers must publish team on-call rotations, on-call handoffs, and escalation points.

2) Roles, career ladders, and leveling overview

Purpose: Our ladders create clear expectations for skills, scope, and promotion criteria across Engineering, Product, Research, and GTM functions. Managers and ICs should use these rubrics for hiring, performance reviews, and development plans.

Career ladder (summary table)

| Role family | Level | Typical years at level | Scope / example expectations | Managerial track? |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| Engineering (SWE) | IC1 (Junior) | 0–2 | Contributes to small features, tests, and bug fixes. Operates under close mentorship. | No |
| Engineering (SWE) | IC2 (Mid) | 2–5 | Delivers features independently, owns components, participates in design reviews. | Optional |
| Engineering (SWE) | IC3 (Senior) | 4–8 | Leads large features, mentors peers, drives architecture in a subdomain. | Optional |
| Engineering (SWE) | Staff / Principal | 7+ | Cross-team initiatives, system design, sets standards and technical strategy. | Optional/Yes |
| Product | PM2–PM4 | 0–8+ | Defines roadmaps, drives product decisions, coordinates cross-functional launches. | Optional/Yes |
| Research/Applied ML | R&D2–R&D4 | 1–8+ | Model evaluation, inference optimization, experimental design, publishes internal evaluations. | Optional/Yes |

Note: The full leveling rubric for each family contains detailed competencies (technical breadth, impact, leadership, scale). See the related 'people-ops-performance-review-process' page for competency matrices and example evidence.

Promotion and performance review highlights

- Cadence: Formal performance reviews occur twice a year (mid-year and year-end). Informal calibration happens quarterly.
- Criteria: Impact, scope, technical execution, cross-team collaboration, mentorship, and company values. Promotion requires demonstrated sustained impact and manager + peer support.
- Evidence: PRs, design docs, incident reviews, customer-impact summaries, and mentorship logs are typical promotion evidence.

3) Benefits and perks (high-level summary)

Redwood offers a competitive benefits package designed to support employees and their families. Below are highlights; for enrollment details, refer to Benefits Portal (People Ops link).

Health & well-being
- Medical, dental, and vision plans with employer contribution.
- Mental health support: licensed therapy through our EAP and dedicated behavioral health coverage.
- Parental leave: 18 weeks primary caregiver leave, 8 weeks secondary caregiver leave (paid). Flexible phased return options available.

Financial & retirement
- Competitive salary bands; annual compensation review and calibration.
- 401(k) with company match after onboarding eligibility period.
- Equity grants for full-time employees; refresh grants considered during performance cycles.

Time off & flexibility
- Generous PTO policy and company-wide holidays.
- Flexible remote work allowances and home office stipend.
- Volunteer time off (VTO) and annual learning stipend.

Development & recognition
- Learning stipend: up to $1,200/year for courses, conferences, and books.
- Internal technical mentorship and apprenticeship programs.
- Quarterly company hack weeks and demo days with awards.

Perks & on-site benefits (where available)
- Commuter stipend in select offices, catered team lunches, and access to quiet rooms.
- Sponsored mental wellness sessions and ergonomic equipment budget.

How to request accommodations or changes

- Submit requests to People Ops via the internal HR portal, email people-ops@redwood.com, or reach out to your manager for immediate needs. All accommodation requests are handled confidentially.

4) Hiring overview — sourcing to offer (high level)

Objective: Conduct efficient, inclusive interviews that surface candidate ability to contribute to Redwood's mission and culture. The full hiring handbook and playbooks live in the Recruiting team space.

High-level steps
1. Requisition and intake: Hiring manager creates a req with JD, level, expected compensation band, and interview packet. People Ops and Recruiting review.
2. Sourcing & screening: Recruiters screen and pass candidates who meet baseline role requirements. Screeners take notes against a rubric.
3. Interview loop: Typical SWE loop: phone screen (culture/behavior + basics), technical exercise (take-home or coding interview), system design (for mid/senior), and final cross-functional sync. Use standardized rubrics for every interviewer.
4. Debrief & calibration: Interviewers submit independent feedback; hiring manager convenes debrief to calibrate and decide.
5. Offer & negotiation: Compensation discussed by People Ops with hiring manager sign-off. Offers include salary, equity, and benefits summary.
6. Onboarding scheduling: Once offer accepted, Recruiting and People Ops coordinate start date, hardware order, and pre-onboarding tasks.

Diversity, equity & inclusion (DEI) in hiring
- Use diverse candidate slates and structured interview rubrics. Interviewers complete unconscious bias training annually. Panels should include at least one trained DEI interviewer where feasible.

5) Onboarding overview — first 90 days and checklist

Purpose: Ensure new hires reach productive independence quickly and feel culturally integrated. The checklist below is the canonical first-90-days plan; managers adapt it to role specifics.

Pre-day-1 (Recruiting & People Ops)
- Send welcome packet, benefits enrollment window, and first-week schedule.
- Order hardware and provision accounts (see Internal tools).

Day 1–7: Foundations
- Orientation session with People Ops: policies, benefits, payroll, and culture.
- Team welcome: meet the manager, skip-level intro, and core teammates.
- Access: confirm accounts for GitHub, Slack, Jira, Confluence, SSO, Okta, VPN, and monitoring dashboards.
- Security & compliance: complete mandatory security training and sign the acceptable-use policy.

Week 2–4: Product and systems onboarding
- Technical onboarding: runtime architecture overview (serving runtime, smart routing, caching), codebase walkthrough, and local dev environment setup.
- Small starter tasks: bug fixes or small features with a buddy/mentor.
- Attend on-call shadow (if applicable) and review incident playbooks.

Month 2–3: Ownership and impact
- Take ownership of a small project or feature and ship it with a release checklist.
- First performance check-in at 30 days; career development plan discussion at 60 days.
- Begin mentorship (as mentee or mentor) and connect to cross-functional partners (product, infra, SRE).

First-90-days checklist (condensed)
- Accounts provisioned: Slack, GitHub, Jira, Confluence, Okta, VPN.
- Local dev environment: passes unit tests and can run local inference tests.
- First change merged to mainline or internal branch with review approvals.
- Security training completed, on-call shadowed if part of team.
- 30/60/90 day check-ins scheduled with manager.

6) Internal tools guide (quick reference)

This section lists core internal tools, owners, and short usage notes. Each item includes the canonical team owner and a short example command or link. For full tool docs, see the respective team spaces.

- Slack — cross-company communications. Owner: People Ops. Use channels: #announcements, #engineering, #sre-oncall.
- GitHub — code, PR reviews, and protected branches. Owner: Eng DevEx. Branch protection: require 2 approvals for main.
- Jira — sprint planning, issue tracking. Owner: Eng Platforms. Use labels: component:, priority:, and release:.
- Confluence — internal documentation and ADRs. Owner: People Ops. Template: design-review-template.
- Okta / SSO — identity and access management. Owner: Security. Provisioning: follow the onboarding checklist ticket.
- Internal CLI (redwoodctl) — developer productivity tool for running local infra and requesting capacity. Example usage:

  redwoodctl env init --project=my-service
  redwoodctl up --profile=developer --gpu=none

- Monitoring & Alerting: Grafana dashboards and PagerDuty. Owner: Eng SRE. On-call runbooks in confluence: 'oncall-and-incident-response/runbooks'.
- Cost & Usage Console — Redwood Console for per-token cost and route analytics. Owner: Product / Eng Platform. Access via internal console link; reviewers must request access for dedicated/private customers.

Provisioning and access flow (summary)
1. Recruiter/People Ops requests accounts via the provisioning ticket system.
2. Okta provision triggers GitHub, Slack, Confluence, and Jira access.
3. Manager verifies access and submits hardware provisioning request to Eng Infra.

7) Manager and mentor responsibilities

Managers should provide clear goals, regular 1:1s, and development plans. Mentors should provide technical pairing, review PRs, and guide career conversations. Expectations: publish 1:1 agendas, provide timely feedback, and ensure psychological safety.

8) Frequently asked questions (select)

Q: Who do I contact for payroll issues?
A: Email finance@redwood.com or open a ticket via the HR portal.

Q: How do I request extended parental leave?
A: Contact People Ops for the leave policy and necessary paperwork; your manager will support an appropriate phased return plan.

Q: Where are incident postmortems stored?
A: In Confluence under 'oncall-and-incident-response/postmortems' with open links from SRE runbooks.

9) Owners, escalation, and maintenance

- Document owner: People Ops (document steward: Ava Martinez).
- Review cadence: Annual review or when policies change (security, benefits, legal).
- Escalation: For ambiguous cases, escalate to Head of People Ops and General Counsel for legal/confidential matters.

Appendix A — Example onboarding CLI snippet

$ # Initialize project environment
$ redwoodctl env init --project=inference-service --region=us-west-2
$ # Start a lightweight local dev stack
$ redwoodctl dev up --gpus=0 --cache=local
